identity.title: A Novel Phenolic From the Heartwood of Cotinus coggygria Scop. With Potential Neuroprotective Effects: In Silico and In Vitro Studies.

content.abstract: Seven known phenolic compounds (2-8) along with one new phenolic compound (1) were isolated from the heartwood of Cotinus coggygria Scop. (Anacardiaceae). Among them, compounds 3-5 are reported from the genus Cotinus for the first time, while compounds 2 and 6-8 are reported from the family Anacardiaceae for the first time. The structure of the new compound was elucidated by detailed spectroscopic analysis, including HR-ESI-MS, 1D, and 2D NMR experiments. In vitro assays showed that compound 1 attenuated glutamate-induced oxidative injury in HT22 cells (EC(50) = 3.852 microM, MTS assay) and inhibited TNF-alpha-induced NF‑kappaB activation in 293T luciferase reporter cells. Molecular docking suggested that compound 1 may bind to IKKbeta, consistent with the observed NF‑kappaB inhibition. Preliminary structure-activity relationship trend analysis indicated that compounds possessing a 6''-O-rhamnose-containing disaccharide moiety (6-8) showed stronger apparent protective activity than the 6''-O -galloyl derivatives (1-5) under the present assay conditions. These preliminary findings suggest that cotinusin A (1) may warrant further investigation for its potential against glutamate-induced oxidative neuronal injury. However, whether the observed NF‑kappaB inhibitory activity translates into anti-neuroinflammatory effects in relevant models remains to be determined, and further mechanistic and in vivo studies are needed to establish its therapeutic potential.
